A plugin format developed by Steinberg that allows software instruments (VST instruments) and effects (VST effects) to be used within a DAW. VST has become the most widely supported plugin format, with thousands of commercial and free instruments and effects available.

See also: DAW, plug-in, synthesis

terms.title: walking bass
terms.short: A bass line of steady quarter notes that outlines the chord changes.
terms.long:
A style of bass accompaniment common in jazz, blues, and Baroque music, consisting of continuous quarter notes that create a feeling of forward motion. <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassline">Walking bass lines</a> use a mixture of chord tones, arpeggios, chromatic runs, and passing tones to outline the chord progression, often with a melodic shape that alternately rises and falls in pitch. The term originates from the footstep-like regularity of the rhythm.

See also: bass line, basso continuo

terms.title: wavetable synthesis
terms.short: A synthesis method that cycles through stored digital waveforms to produce sound.
terms.long:
A digital synthesis technique in which a stored table of single-cycle waveforms is read repeatedly to produce a tone. What distinguishes wavetable synthesis from simple sampling is the ability to morph or scan through multiple waveforms over time, creating evolving timbres. Invented by Max Mathews in 1958 and developed for hardware synthesizers by Wolfgang Palm (PPG) in the late 1970s, the technique became ubiquitous in software synthesis through instruments such as Native Instruments Massive and Xfer Serum.

See also: subtractive synthesis, FM synthesis, granular synthesis

terms.title: wet/dry signal
terms.short: Dry = unprocessed audio; wet = audio with effects applied.
terms.long:
A dry signal is the original, unprocessed audio as captured or generated before any effects are applied. A wet signal is that same audio after passing through one or more effects processors — reverb, delay, chorus, distortion, etc. In most effects units and plugins, a wet/dry (or mix) knob blends the two, allowing the producer to dial in the amount of effect without replacing the source sound entirely.

See also: reverb, effects, signal processing

terms.title: 12-bar blues
terms.short: A repeating 12-measure harmonic framework foundational to blues, jazz, and rock.
terms.long:
A repeating harmonic and formal pattern of twelve bars that is the foundational framework of blues music and has influenced jazz, rhythm and blues, rock and roll, and country. The basic form uses three chords: I (bars 1–4), IV (bars 5–6), I (bars 7–8), V (bar 9), IV (bar 10), I (bars 11–12). Countless variations exist, particularly in jazz (the "rhythm changes" is a contrasting alternative).

See also: blues scale, riff, form

tok.q: When the blues is taught as a fixed twelve-bar pattern, whose version of the blues becomes the standard?

terms.title: 12-note techniques
terms.short: A compositional method using a fixed ordering of all twelve chromatic pitches as the basis for a piece.
terms.long:
A compositional method developed by Arnold Schoenberg in the early 1920s in which all twelve chromatic pitches are arranged into a fixed ordered series (tone row or set). The row and its three transformations — inversion (I), retrograde (R), and retrograde inversion (RI) — form the exclusive pitch material of the piece. Adopted and developed by Webern and Berg (the Second Viennese School) and later by Stravinsky, Dallapiccola, and others.

See also: atonal, retrograde, inversion

terms.title: VII
terms.short: The seventh scale degree or a chord built on it.
terms.long: In Roman numeral analysis, VII (or vii°) denotes the seventh degree of the scale and the chord built on it. In major keys, the seventh degree is a leading tone a half step below the tonic; the triad built on it is diminished. Uppercase numerals indicate major quality; lowercase indicate minor.

terms.title: VI
terms.short: The sixth scale degree or a chord built on it.
terms.long: VI denotes the sixth scale degree (the submediant) and the chord built on it. In major keys, this chord is minor (vi); when written in uppercase (VI), it refers to a major chord on the sixth degree, common in minor keys and as a chromatic alteration.

terms.title: IV
terms.short: The subdominant — the fourth scale degree or a chord built on it.
terms.long: IV denotes the subdominant — the fourth degree of the scale. The subdominant chord moves naturally toward either the dominant (V) or directly to the tonic (I), the latter producing a plagal cadence.

terms.title: V
terms.short: The dominant — the fifth scale degree or a chord built on it.
terms.long: V denotes the dominant — the fifth degree of the scale and the most harmonically active chord in tonal music. The dominant triad (V) or seventh chord (V7) creates strong tension that resolves to the tonic (I). The V–I progression is the foundation of tonal cadential motion.

terms.title: III
terms.short: The mediant — the third scale degree or a chord built on it.
terms.long: III denotes the mediant — the third degree of the scale, midway between the tonic and dominant. In major keys the mediant chord is minor (iii); uppercase III refers to a major chord on the third degree, typical in minor keys.

terms.title: II
terms.short: The supertonic — the second scale degree or a chord built on it.
terms.long: II denotes the supertonic — the second degree of the scale. In major keys, the supertonic chord is minor (ii) and functions as a pre-dominant, often preceding V. The II chord (uppercase, major) appears frequently as a secondary dominant or in modal contexts.

terms.title: I
terms.short: The tonic — the home chord, built on the first scale degree.
terms.long: I denotes the tonic — the first scale degree and the chord built on it. The tonic chord is the harmonic center of gravity in tonal music; most pieces begin and end on I. In major keys it is a major triad; in minor keys it is minor (i).

terms.title: Aesthetics
terms.short: Aesthetics deals with the characteristics, creation, meaning and perception of beauty and taste.
terms.long:
Aesthetics deals with the characteristics, creation, meaning and perception of beauty and taste. The study of aesthetics develops skills for the critical appreciation and analysis of art, culture and nature.

In the arts: The concept of aesthetics is perceived differently around the world and across cultures. In the arts, aesthetics may begin with the formal study of the elements of art and beauty but should also include diverse cultural perspectives.

tok.q: How are artistic standards developed and maintained?

terms.title: Change
terms.short: Change is a conversion, transformation or movement from one form, state or value to another.
terms.long:
Change is a conversion, transformation or movement from one form, state or value to another. Inquiry into the concept of change involves understanding and evaluating causes, processes and consequences.

In the arts: The arts may be a reflection of change, or an inspiration for change. Change may be considered as external to the arts or incorporated within an artwork. In the arts, change can also be termed as metamorphosis or transformation—a marked change in appearance, form, nature or character.

terms.title: Communication
terms.short: Communication is the exchange or transfer of signals, facts, ideas and symbols.
terms.long:
Communication is the exchange or transfer of signals, facts, ideas and symbols. It requires a sender, a message and an intended receiver. Communication involves the activity of conveying information or meaning. Effective communication requires a common "language" (which may be written, spoken or non-verbal).

In the arts: Communication is often regarded in the arts as a message between the artist and an audience, or between performers. Without intended communication the arts become solely self-expressive. An artistic intention is the artist's communication of the intended impact of the artwork/performance on an audience. Communication is also key to collaboration, to presenting and negotiating ideas and to giving feedback. Communication in the arts can occur through a variety of media—through artifacts, the body, image, movement, sound, text, visuals and voice.

terms.title: Communities
terms.short: Communities are groups that exist in proximity defined by space, time or relationship.
terms.long: Communities are groups that exist in proximity defined by space, time or relationship. Communities include, for example, groups of people sharing particular characteristics, beliefs or values as well as groups of interdependent organisms living together in a specific habitat.

terms.title: Connections
terms.short: Connections are links, bonds and relationships among people, objects, organisms or ideas.
terms.long: Connections are links, bonds and relationships among people, objects, organisms or ideas.

terms.title: Creativity
terms.short: Creativity is the process of generating novel ideas and considering existing ideas from new perspectives.
terms.long: Creativity is the process of generating novel ideas and considering existing ideas from new perspectives. Creativity includes the ability to recognize the value of ideas when developing innovative responses to problems; it may be evident in process as well as outcomes, products or solutions.

terms.title: Culture
terms.short: Culture encompasses a range of learned and shared beliefs, values, interests, attitudes, products, ways of knowing and patterns of behaviour created by human communities.
terms.long:
Culture encompasses a range of learned and shared beliefs, values, interests, attitudes, products, ways of knowing and patterns of behaviour created by human communities. The concept of culture is dynamic and organic.

TOK: Shared practices, values, and beliefs of a community that shape how knowledge is produced and understood.

terms.title: Global interactions
terms.short: Global interactions, as a concept, focuses on the connections between individuals and communities, as well as their relationships with built and natural environments, from the perspective of the world as a whole.
terms.long: Global interactions, as a concept, focuses on the connections between individuals and communities, as well as their relationships with built and natural environments, from the perspective of the world as a whole.

terms.title: Identity
terms.short: Identity refers to the particular features that define individuals, groups, things, eras, places, symbols and styles.
terms.long:
Identity refers to the particular features that define individuals, groups, things, eras, places, symbols and styles. Identity can be observed, or it can be constructed, asserted and shaped by external and internal influences.

In the arts: In the arts, we often explore the self and self-discovery through the concept of identity; however, identity may also be related to the identification of a genre, style, movement, particular artist or place. The arts often give us insights into the identity of a culture or a period of time, providing us with an idea of how a culture identifies itself and of the characteristics and values of a culture.

terms.title: Logic
terms.short: Logic is a method of reasoning and a system of principles used to build arguments and reach conclusions.
terms.long: Logic is a method of reasoning and a system of principles used to build arguments and reach conclusions.

terms.title: Perspective
terms.short: Perspective is the position from which we observe situations, objects, facts, ideas and opinions.
terms.long:
Perspective is the position from which we observe situations, objects, facts, ideas and opinions. Perspective may be associated with individuals, groups, cultures or disciplines. Different perspectives often lead to multiple representations and interpretations.

TOK: A particular position or angle from which knowledge is viewed. All knowers have a perspective.

terms.title: Relationships
terms.short: Relationships are the connections and associations between properties, objects, people and ideas—including the human community's connections with the world in which we live.
terms.long: Relationships are the connections and associations between properties, objects, people and ideas—including the human community's connections with the world in which we live. Any change in relationship brings consequences—some of which may occur on a small scale, while others may be far reaching, affecting large networks and systems such as human societies and the planetary ecosystem.

terms.title: Systems
terms.short: Systems are sets of interacting or interdependent components.
terms.long: Systems are sets of interacting or interdependent components. Systems provide structure and order in human, natural and built environments. Systems can be static or dynamic, simple or complex.

terms.title: Time, place and space
terms.short: The intrinsically linked concept of time, place and space refers to the absolute or relative position of people, objects and ideas.
terms.long: The intrinsically linked concept of time, place and space refers to the absolute or relative position of people, objects and ideas. Time, place and space focuses on how we construct and use our understanding of location ("where" and "when").

terms.title: Audience
terms.short: An individual or group who receive and/or respond to arts.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept: An individual or group who receive and/or respond to arts. Addressing this concept includes examining strategies for engaging audience, different types of audiences and how the audience–artist relationship affects and influences the arts.

terms.title: Boundaries
terms.short: The parameters that define a personality, a culture, an environment, civil law, a skill set or a belief structure.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept: The parameters that define a personality, a culture, an environment, civil law, a skill set or a belief structure. The concept of boundaries can include: themes, issues and concepts; the imagined or physical boundary between performance space and audience; the subversive or provocative nature of the arts; the dividing line between what is real and what is fictional; private and public space; the relationships between characters.

terms.title: Composition
terms.short: The intentional organization or contrast, balance, arrangement or awareness of the principles of art for a particular purpose in the creation of art.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept: The intentional organization or contrast, balance, arrangement or awareness of the principles of art for a particular purpose in the creation of art. These may include tension and release, repetition and variety, unison and harmony, sound and silence, theme and variation, and dynamics and energy.

terms.title: Expression
terms.short: The representation of feelings and emotions, ideas, thoughts, beliefs, values and opinions in the process of visual or physical articulation.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept: The representation of feelings and emotions, ideas, thoughts, beliefs, values and opinions in the process of visual or physical articulation. It can include signs, symbols, semiotics or any other imagery to capture the artistic intention. It is something you do, create or play that shows what you think or feel. Expression may facilitate the communication of an idea.

terms.title: Genre
terms.short: A type or category of art that can be identified through a particular set of characteristics, techniques and/or conventions.
terms.long:
MYP Arts related concept: A type or category of art that can be identified through a particular set of characteristics, techniques and/or conventions. The features may, of course, vary between arts disciplines and art forms.

A study of genres includes essential understandings about conventions of genre as applied to the different arts disciplines: for example, form, style, tone, mood, atmosphere, composition, instrumentation, choreography, rhythm, movement, costume, lighting, and so on.

Examples of genres include tragedy, melodrama, jazz, blues, satire, pop art.

tok.q: Who draws the boundaries of a genre: musicians, listeners, scholars or the music industry?

terms.title: Innovation
terms.short: An altered interpretation of, or experimentation with, ideas, techniques and media.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept: An altered interpretation of, or experimentation with, ideas, techniques and media. It promotes originality and creativity through new ways of presenting ideas and unusual use of media.

terms.title: Interpretation
terms.short: The understanding of an artwork's meaning, as determined by the context of the artist, artwork or audience.
terms.long:
MYP Arts related concept: The understanding of an artwork's meaning, as determined by the context of the artist, artwork or audience.

A distinctive personal performance or re-creation of an existing artwork.

TOK concept: The act of explaining or making sense of knowledge or meaning. Opposite of misunderstanding.

tok.q: To what extent should there be variations in interpretation of a piece of music? Is it valid if one listener perceives a piece of music to be "sad" while another listener perceives the same piece of music as "happy"?

terms.title: Narrative
terms.short: A spoken, written or visual account of connected events; a story, which may be fictional or non-fictional.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept: A spoken, written or visual account of connected events; a story, which may be fictional or non-fictional.

terms.title: Play
terms.short: Play can occur in an artistic process or product.
terms.long:
MYP Arts related concept (performing arts): Play can occur in an artistic process or product.

In process, play is experimentation—playing with ideas, characters and techniques. This may be structured or free play.

Improvisation is a form of structured play that can also be presented as performance.

In product, play can be a collective creation of a theatre piece or a pre-existing piece of theatre that is authored and documented, and that is transformed into live action.

terms.title: Presentation
terms.short: The choice of medium, tool and exhibition or performance space that contributes to audience understanding of the meaning or purpose of the artwork.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept: The choice of medium, tool and exhibition or performance space that contributes to audience understanding of the meaning or purpose of the artwork.

terms.title: Representation
terms.short: The description, depiction or portrayal of a person, group, place or item in a particular way or as being of a particular nature.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept (visual arts): The description, depiction or portrayal of a person, group, place or item in a particular way or as being of a particular nature. An image or likeness.

terms.title: Role
terms.short: The development, adoption and portrayal of a character or style by a performer.
terms.long:
MYP Arts related concept (performing arts): The development, adoption and portrayal of a character or style by a performer. Different approaches, ideas and texts can be used to influence the presentation of character or style.

Role can also refer to the different responsibilities related to the presentation and performance of an artwork, such as lighting, sound, direction/conducting, choreography.

terms.title: Structure
terms.short: This refers to the shape, timing and organization of the art and the factors that determine how a piece or performance is shaped.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept (performing arts): This refers to the shape, timing and organization of the art and the factors that determine how a piece or performance is shaped. It takes into consideration form, function, narrative, melody, harmony, contrast, focus and the construction of smaller parts to create a whole.

terms.title: Style
terms.short: A type of art characteristic of a group of people, a person or period of time and belonging to a shared tradition or set of conventions.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept (visual arts): A type of art characteristic of a group of people, a person or period of time and belonging to a shared tradition or set of conventions. Art conforming to an established form. The distinctive way in which something is made or presented.

terms.title: Visual culture
terms.short: A field of study that generally includes some combination of cultural studies, art history, critical theory, philosophy and anthropology by focusing on aspects of culture that rely on visual images.
terms.long: MYP Arts related concept (visual arts): A field of study that generally includes some combination of cultural studies, art history, critical theory, philosophy and anthropology by focusing on aspects of culture that rely on visual images.

terms.title: Knowledge claim
terms.short: Any assertion that something is true or that one knows something.
terms.long: TOK: Any assertion that something is true or that one knows something. Whenever we say we know something, we are making a knowledge claim.

terms.title: Knower
terms.short: The person (or group) who holds knowledge.
terms.long: TOK: The person (or group) who holds knowledge. TOK asks us to reflect on how the knower's perspective, background, and method shape what is known.

terms.title: Personal knowledge
terms.short: Knowledge that depends on the individual's own experience, insight, or skill — difficult to transfer directly to others.
terms.long: TOK: Knowledge that depends on the individual's own experience, insight, or skill — difficult to transfer directly to others.

terms.title: Shared knowledge
terms.short: Knowledge that is developed, tested, and held collectively by a community or discipline.
terms.long: TOK: Knowledge that is developed, tested, and held collectively by a community or discipline.

terms.title: Experiential knowledge
terms.short: Knowledge gained through direct personal experience rather than reasoning or testimony.
terms.long: TOK: Knowledge gained through direct personal experience rather than reasoning or testimony.

terms.title: Procedural knowledge
terms.short: Knowing how to do something; practical, skill-based knowledge (sometimes called "know-how").
terms.long: TOK: Knowing how to do something; practical, skill-based knowledge (sometimes called "know-how").

tok.q: Is kinaesthetic learning a way to acquire knowledge?

terms.title: Propositional knowledge
terms.short: Knowing that something is the case; factual knowledge expressed as a statement (sometimes called "know-that").
terms.long: TOK: Knowing that something is the case; factual knowledge expressed as a statement (sometimes called "know-that").

terms.title: Evidence
terms.short: Information or data that supports or challenges a knowledge claim.
terms.long: TOK: Information or data that supports or challenges a knowledge claim.

terms.title: Certainty
terms.short: The degree of confidence we have that a knowledge claim is true.
terms.long: TOK: The degree of confidence we have that a knowledge claim is true. Opposite of doubt.

terms.title: Truth
terms.short: A claim that corresponds to reality or is universally valid.
terms.long: TOK: A claim that corresponds to reality or is universally valid. Opposite of falsehood.

terms.title: Power
terms.short: The ability to influence what is accepted as knowledge.
terms.long: TOK: The ability to influence what is accepted as knowledge. Knowledge and power are closely linked.

terms.title: Justification
terms.short: Reasoning that shows why a knowledge claim is valid.
terms.long: TOK: Reasoning that shows why a knowledge claim is valid. What distinguishes a good justification from a bad one?

terms.title: Explanation
terms.short: A statement that clarifies why something is the way it is, resolving a puzzle or gap in understanding.
terms.long: TOK: A statement that clarifies why something is the way it is, resolving a puzzle or gap in understanding.

terms.title: Objectivity
terms.short: Seeing or producing knowledge without personal or cultural bias; independent of the observer.
terms.long: TOK: Seeing or producing knowledge without personal or cultural bias; independent of the observer.

terms.title: Values
terms.short: Principles or standards of behaviour that guide how knowledge is used and what counts as worthwhile.
terms.long: TOK: Principles or standards of behaviour that guide how knowledge is used and what counts as worthwhile.

terms.title: Responsibility
terms.short: The duties knowers have in creating, sharing, and applying knowledge.
terms.long: TOK: The duties knowers have in creating, sharing, and applying knowledge. Where does responsibility begin and end?

terms.title: Bias
terms.short: A systematic distortion of the truth — often present in how data are selected, presented, or interpreted.
terms.long: TOK: A systematic distortion of the truth — often present in how data are selected, presented, or interpreted.

terms.title: Subjectivity
terms.short: In aesthetic judgment, drawing on features of the observer (personal taste, emotional response) rather than features of the artwork itself.
terms.long: TOK: In aesthetic judgment, drawing on features of the observer (personal taste, emotional response) rather than features of the artwork itself.

terms.title: Aesthetic value
terms.short: The quality of an artwork that makes it meaningful, beautiful, or significant — debated as partly subjective and partly objective.
terms.long: TOK: The quality of an artwork that makes it meaningful, beautiful, or significant — debated as partly subjective and partly objective.

tok.q: Are certain ways of knowing employed in radically different ways in the arts as opposed to other areas of knowledge?

terms.title: Primary source
terms.short: A document, object, or testimony produced at the time of the events under study.
terms.long: TOK: A document, object, or testimony produced at the time of the events under study.

tok.q: When a musician describes their own work in an interview, how much should that count as evidence of what the music means?

terms.title: Secondary source
terms.short: An account or analysis produced after the events, drawing on primary sources and other evidence.
terms.long: TOK: An account or analysis produced after the events, drawing on primary sources and other evidence.

terms.title: Academic integrity
terms.short: The set of norms governing honest knowledge production: accurate data collection and reporting, proper attribution, transparency about methods and limitations, and resistance to pressure to exaggerate or fabricate results.
terms.long: TOK: The set of norms governing honest knowledge production: accurate data collection and reporting, proper attribution, transparency about methods and limitations, and resistance to pressure to exaggerate or fabricate results.

terms.title: Identify
terms.short: Recognize and state briefly a distinguishing fact or feature.
terms.long:
MYP: Recognize and state briefly a distinguishing fact or feature.

DP Music (achievement level 1, research and written work): Provide an answer from a number of possibilities.

terms.title: Outline
terms.short: Give a brief account or summary.
terms.long: MYP and DP Music (achievement level 1): Give a brief account or summary.

terms.title: State
terms.short: Give a specific name, value or other brief answer without explanation or calculation.
terms.long: MYP: Give a specific name, value or other brief answer without explanation or calculation. The first rung for artistic choices (Bii).

terms.title: Describe
terms.short: Give a detailed account or picture of a situation, event, pattern or process.
terms.long:
MYP: Give a detailed account or picture of a situation, event, pattern or process. The top band in MYP1 for Aii, Bii and Dii; from MYP2 it earns only 5–6.

DP Music (achievement level 2): Give a detailed account.

terms.title: Analyse
terms.short: Break down in order to bring out the essential elements or structure.
terms.long: MYP: Break down in order to bring out the essential elements or structure. (To identify parts and relationships, and interpret information to reach conclusions.) The top band in MYP2–3 for Aii and Dii, and in MYP1 for Di.

terms.title: Explain
terms.short: Give a detailed account including reasons or causes.
terms.long:
MYP: Give a detailed account including reasons or causes. The top band in MYP2–3 for Bii ("… because …").

DP Music (achievement level 3): Give a detailed account, including reasons or causes.

terms.title: Justify
terms.short: Give valid reasons or evidence to support an answer or conclusion.
terms.long: MYP and DP Music (achievement level 3): Give valid reasons or evidence to support an answer or conclusion. The top band in MYP4–5 for Bii. A justified choice names the specific action (what, where in the piece, how) and a reason that can be checked.

tok.q: What makes a reason for an artistic choice "valid", and who decides?

terms.title: Evaluate
terms.short: Make an appraisal by weighing up the strengths and limitations.
terms.long: MYP and DP Music (achievement level 4): Make an appraisal by weighing up the strengths and limitations. The top band in MYP2–3 for Di; in MYP4–5 the top band asks you to evaluate "thoroughly and perceptively": say why each thing works or fails for a listener, not only that it does.

tok.q: How do artistic judgments differ from other types of judgment, such as moral judgments?

terms.title: Critique
terms.short: Provide a critical review or commentary, especially when dealing with works of art or literature.
terms.long: MYP: Provide a critical review or commentary, especially when dealing with works of art or literature. The top band in MYP4–5 for Aii: judge which artistic choices work and which do not, and tie every judgment to a specific moment in the piece.

tok.q: Can a critique be objective when it rests on the critic's taste? What would make it more than opinion?

terms.title: Discuss
terms.short: Offer a considered and balanced review that includes a range of arguments, factors or hypotheses.
terms.long:
MYP: Offer a considered and balanced review that includes a range of arguments, factors or hypotheses. Opinions or conclusions should be presented clearly and supported by appropriate evidence. The top band in MYP4–5 for Dii.

DP Music (achievement level 4): Offer a considered and balanced review supported by appropriate evidence.

terms.title: List
terms.short: Give a sequence of brief answers with no explanation.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 1, research and written work): Give a sequence of brief answers with no explanation.

terms.title: Assemble
terms.short: Combine or gather pre-existing material without change.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 1, practical work): Combine or gather pre-existing material without change.

terms.title: Approximate
terms.short: Imitate with lack of detail.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 1, practical work): Imitate with lack of detail.

terms.title: Reiterate
terms.short: Repeat or restate, largely without change.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 1, practical work): Repeat or restate, largely without change.

terms.title: Demonstrate
terms.short: Make clear by reasoning or evidence, illustrating with examples or practical application.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 2): Make clear by reasoning or evidence, illustrating with examples or practical application.

terms.title: Distinguish
terms.short: Make clear the differences between two or more concepts or items.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 2): Make clear the differences between two or more concepts or items.

terms.title: Exhibit
terms.short: Demonstrate a characteristic in the appropriate context.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 2, practical work): Demonstrate a characteristic in the appropriate context.

terms.title: Transmit
terms.short: Give a formulaic rendition of an existing work or style.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 2, practical work): Give a formulaic rendition of an existing work or style.

terms.title: Recreate
terms.short: Produce a representation of an original.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 2, practical work): Produce a representation of an original.

terms.title: Investigate
terms.short: Observe, study or make a detailed and systematic examination in order to establish facts and reach new conclusions.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 3): Observe, study or make a detailed and systematic examination in order to establish facts and reach new conclusions. In the MYP, Criterion A is "Investigating".

terms.title: Realize
terms.short: Plan and create a work according to convention or practice.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 3, practical work): Plan and create a work according to convention or practice.

terms.title: Shape
terms.short: Modify and develop existing material.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 3, practical work): Modify and develop existing material.

terms.title: Adapt
terms.short: Adjust existing material to suit a new context or style.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 3, practical work): Adjust existing material to suit a new context or style. Exploring music in context asks for "one performed adaptation of music from a local or global context for the student's own instrument".

terms.title: Examine
terms.short: Consider an argument or concept in a way that uncovers the assumptions and interrelationships of the issue.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 4): Consider an argument or concept in a way that uncovers the assumptions and interrelationships of the issue.

terms.title: Personalize
terms.short: Bring personal ideas and interpretations to a work or practice.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 4, practical work): Bring personal ideas and interpretations to a work or practice.

terms.title: Synthesize
terms.short: Combine and blend existing elements, styles or techniques to create new work.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 4, practical work): Combine and blend existing elements, styles or techniques to create new work.

terms.title: Transform
terms.short: Change and develop existing work to create new work.
terms.long: DP Music (achievement level 4, practical work): Change and develop existing work to create new work.

terms.title: Criterion A: Investigating
terms.short: Research a genre or movement (Ai) and respond to one piece from it (Aii).
terms.long: Ai: investigate a genre or movement, related to the statement of inquiry. Aii: respond to one artwork or performance from the genre. Research, not opinion and not biography; one piece, judged from detail. See the pathway for what each year adds.

terms.title: Criterion B: Developing
terms.short: Explore ideas in practice (Bi) and state an artistic intention with your choices (Bii).
terms.long: Bi: practically explore ideas, with evidence from the beginning, the middle and towards the end of the process. Develop ideas, do not only present them. Bii: present a clear artistic intention in line with the statement of inquiry, written before the work, with reasons for each choice.

terms.title: Criterion C: Creating/Performing
terms.short: Create or perform the finished work.
terms.long: The descriptor wording is the same in every year; the rise comes from the harder skills each unit teaches.

terms.title: Criterion D: Evaluating
terms.short: Appraise the finished work (Di) and reflect on how you changed as a musician (Dii).
terms.long: Di: appraise the finished work, not the process. Dii: say explicitly how you changed as a musician: what you could not do, what you can do now, and what caused the change.

terms.title: Statement of inquiry
terms.short: The sentence that joins a unit's key concept, related concepts and global context into one idea to explore.
terms.long: Every MYP unit has one. In music, Ai connects the genre to it, and Bii's artistic intention says how your work connects to it.

terms.title: Global context (MYP)
terms.short: One of six MYP lenses that set a unit in the wider world.
terms.long: The six MYP global contexts are identities and relationships; orientation in space and time; personal and cultural expression; scientific and technical innovation; globalization and sustainability; fairness and development. Not the same thing as the DP's global context, which is about music unfamiliar to you.

terms.title: Artistic intention
terms.short: What you mean your work to do, for whom, and why, stated before the work is finished.
terms.long: MYP1 begins with a sentence: "My artistic intention is to perform … so that …. This connects to the statement of inquiry because …." Each year adds to it: reasons (MYP2), a justified choice per element (MYP4), purpose, mood and audience (MYP4–5). In the DP the same idea runs through the experimentation report's rationale and the contemporary music-maker's artistic vision.

tok.q: If a listener hears something in your piece that you did not intend, is it still in the piece?

terms.title: ePortfolio
terms.short: The MYP5 arts eAssessment: one unit's work in all four criteria, submitted to the IB and moderated.
terms.long: Optional; MYP4 students decide whether to take it in MYP5. Every unit from MYP1 on is built as a small version of it (Task 1 = A, Task 2 = B, Task 3 = C, Task 4 = D), and the first MYP5 unit is a full practice run. The file types and limits for the practice run are still to be confirmed from the current guide.

terms.title: Area of inquiry
terms.short: One of four ways the DP course groups music by what it is for.
terms.long: The four areas are a framework, not a fixed list of genres: one genre may be explored through more than one area. "In each area, students should consider musical intentions and purposes, the methods and techniques used to create the music, the role of musical conventions, and the impact and experience of the audience." Students spread their attention equally across the areas and contexts.

tok.q: What, if anything, do the different subjects that make up the arts have in common?

terms.title: Area of inquiry 1: Music for sociocultural and political expression
terms.short: Music that expresses social and cultural messages, conveys political ideas or preserves traditions.
terms.long: The guide's examples: protest songs, liturgical music, national anthems.

terms.title: Area of inquiry 2: Music for listening and performance
terms.short: Music that expresses and communicates intrinsic aesthetic values, sometimes called "absolute music".
terms.long: The guide's examples: chamber music of the Western art tradition, cool jazz, experimental music.

terms.title: Area of inquiry 3: Music for dramatic impact, movement and entertainment
terms.short: Music for dramatic effect, for choreographed movement or dance, or meant to entertain.
terms.long: The guide's examples: music for film, music for ballet, musical theatre.

terms.title: Area of inquiry 4: Music technology in the electronic and digital age
terms.short: Music created, performed or produced with electronic or digital technologies.
terms.long: The guide's examples: electronic dance music, Elektronische Musik, technology in popular music production.

tok.q: To what extent does technology enhance and hinder creativity?

terms.title: Personal context
terms.short: Music that matters to you and that you know best.
terms.long: "Students consider their immediate cultural context and interests that contribute to their emerging musical identity."

terms.title: Local context
terms.short: Music with local significance that may be unfamiliar to you.
terms.long: Music from your local, regional or cultural communities, including music you are not currently engaged with.

terms.title: Global context
terms.short: Unfamiliar music from a variety of places, societies and cultures.
terms.long: It may be from a distant region, or nearby but not previously accessible to you. Not the same as the MYP's global contexts.

tok.q: To what extent does context have an impact on musical developments, and vice versa?
Can you understand music from an unfamiliar culture without learning that culture's own words for it?

terms.title: Exploring music in context
terms.short: DP component: a portfolio of written work and practical exercises from contrasting contexts and at least two areas of inquiry.
terms.long: External; SL 30%, HL 20%. Up to 2,400 words of written work, one creating exercise (score up to 32 bars and/or audio up to 1 minute) and one performed adaptation of music from a local or global context for your own instrument (up to 2 minutes).

terms.title: Experimenting with music
terms.short: DP component: a report with evidence of creating and performing experiments in two areas of inquiry.
terms.long: Internal; SL 30%, HL 20%. A written experimentation report (up to 1,500 words) giving a rationale and commentary, with three related excerpts of creating and three of performing (up to 5 minutes each). It grows straight out of MYP Criterion B.

tok.q: How is knowledge constructed through artistic processes and actions?
Why might we be more concerned with process rather than product in the search for knowledge?

terms.title: Presenting music
terms.short: DP component: programme notes, a composition or improvisation, and a performance, across the four areas of inquiry.
terms.long: External; SL 40%, HL 30%. Programme notes (up to 600 words), composition and/or improvisation (up to 6 minutes), solo and/or ensemble performance (up to 12 minutes).

tok.q: To what extent does a composer control the perception of a composition after the composition is completed?

terms.title: The contemporary music-maker
terms.short: HL only: a real-life music project, planned and made with other students, presented as a multimedia presentation.
terms.long: Internal; HL 30%. A continuous multimedia presentation (up to 15 minutes) of the project proposal, the process and evaluation, and the realized project or selections from it. "The music project must involve other students who will work in collaboration with the student." HL students are encouraged to start researching possible projects from the start of the course. Often shortened to CMM.

tok.q: To what extent does "limitation" influence creativity?

terms.title: Higher level (HL)
terms.short: The same DP Music course as SL, plus the contemporary music-maker project.
terms.long: SL weightings: Exploring 30%, Experimenting 30%, Presenting 40%. HL: Exploring 20%, Experimenting 20%, Presenting 30%, contemporary music-maker 30%. This is the course first assessed in 2022; a new DP Music course starts in fall 2028, and its details are not known here yet.

terms.title: Researcher
terms.short: DP musical role: investigating music through aural, kinaesthetic and scholarly research.
terms.long: "Students will engage with primary and secondary sources to collect findings that inform their understanding of music and its place within history and culture. Students present their findings in musical ways and explain their understanding using accurate terminology."

tok.q: Is a recording a primary source for a piece of music, or only for one performance of it?

terms.title: Creator
terms.short: DP musical role: making music by composing, improvising and arranging.
terms.long: Created work is presented "through recorded performances, digitally created tracks and appropriate forms of notation".

tok.q: What moral responsibilities do composers have?
To what extent does knowledge of creative process have an impact on one's perception of a piece of music?

terms.title: Performer
terms.short: DP musical role: practical music-making, including interpretation, expression and technical proficiency.
terms.long: "All three musical roles are of equal value and should not be taught in isolation throughout the course."

tok.q: Can a performance of older music be "authentic" when nobody alive heard the original?

terms.title: Programme notes
terms.short: Up to 600 words presenting your work as a researcher, in Presenting music.

terms.title: Uninformed imitation
terms.short: DP achievement level 1: existing material replicated without direction or sense of purpose.
terms.long: "The student replicates existing material without direction and sense of purpose; musical material is taken out of context or misrepresented." Terms at this level: identify, list, outline, assemble, approximate, reiterate.

terms.title: Precise imitation
terms.short: DP achievement level 2: technically accurate, but without personal musical choices.
terms.long: "The work constructs a recognizable original or rearranges existing material. The work is technically accurate but lacks evidence of personal musical choices." Terms: describe, demonstrate, distinguish, exhibit, transmit, recreate.

terms.title: Informed proficiency
terms.short: DP achievement level 3: technically proficient, realizing conventions, with informed choices.
terms.long: "The student's work is technically proficient and realizes musical conventions and practices. The student adapts material and makes informed technical choices." Terms: explain, investigate, justify, realize, shape, adapt.

terms.title: Mastery and resourcefulness
terms.short: DP achievement level 4: a distinctive, personal voice shown through technical and musical accomplishment.
terms.long: "The student's musical work expresses a distinctive, personal voice manifested through technical and musical accomplishment." Terms: discuss, examine, evaluate, synthesize, personalize, transform.

terms.title: Audiation
terms.short: Hearing and understanding music in your mind when the sound is not there.
terms.long: Gordon: "Audiation is to music what thought is to language" (Introduction). It is "the process of assimilating and comprehending (not simply rehearing) music momentarily heard performed or heard sometime in the past", and also happens when reading, composing or improvising (p. 3). Imitation is not audiation: "Imitation is learning through someone else's ears. Audiation is learning through one's own ears" (p. 9).

tok.q: Gordon writes that the meaning we give to sounds differs from person to person. If two people audiate the same melody differently, is one of them wrong?

terms.title: Tonal pattern
terms.short: Two to five pitches heard as one unit, like a word in language.
terms.long: "Just as a word is the basic unit of meaning in language, so a pattern is the basic unit of meaning in music" (p. 99). Students first learn patterns of "at least two but not more than five pitches corresponding to important functions in a tonality", such as tonic and dominant (p. 100). Tonal patterns are learned apart from rhythm, every pitch the same length.

terms.title: Rhythm pattern
terms.short: A group of durations heard as one unit, organized around macrobeats and microbeats.
terms.long: Learned apart from pitch, chanted on one pitch with expressive inflection (p. 101).

terms.title: Resting tone
terms.short: The pitch a melody feels at rest on; it tells you the tonality.
terms.long: In MLT, tonality is heard from its resting tone, not read from a key signature (p. 150).

tok.q: Music Learning Theory, classical theory and jazz can each name the mode of the same notes differently. Can all three be right?

terms.title: Macrobeat
terms.short: The longer, stronger beats you feel the music moving in; their grouping gives the meter.
terms.long: Macrobeats divided into two microbeats give usual duple meter; into three, usual triple (pp. 175–176).

terms.title: Microbeat
terms.short: The equal divisions of a macrobeat: two in duple meter, three in triple.

terms.title: Skill learning sequence
terms.short: Gordon's order for learning music skills: from hearing and singing, to naming, to reading, to inventing and explaining.
terms.long: Two kinds of learning. Discrimination learning (you are taught): aural/oral, verbal association, partial synthesis, symbolic association, composite synthesis. Inference learning (you teach yourself from what you know): generalization, creativity/improvisation, theoretical understanding. Students move up step by step, and may bridge across to inference levels once ready (Table 17, p. 230). On this site the enrichment options are tagged with these levels.

terms.title: Discrimination learning
terms.short: The levels of skill learning where you are taught: learning by rote, then naming, reading and writing what you know.

terms.title: Inference learning
terms.short: The levels of skill learning where you teach yourself unfamiliar music from what you already know.
terms.long: "It is impossible to teach students all patterns they will ultimately need to know … by relying on discrimination learning alone" (p. 106).

terms.title: Aural/oral
terms.short: MLT level 1: hear patterns and sing or chant them back on a neutral syllable, with no names or notation.
terms.long: A pause comes between the teacher's pattern and the student's answer, "because without a pause, students are encouraged to imitate, not audiate" (p. 102). Scales, names, notation and theory come later (pp. 101–102).

terms.title: Verbal association
terms.short: MLT level 2: put names on patterns you can already audiate: tonal and rhythm syllables, then names like major or duple.
terms.long: Movable do with a la-based minor, and rhythm syllables based on beat functions (p. 105). Sounds are taught first, then syllables as names for what has already been heard (p. 107).

terms.title: Partial synthesis
terms.short: MLT level 3: recognize the tonality or meter of a series of familiar patterns, with no context given first.
terms.long: The teacher uses a neutral syllable so that students find the tonality or meter through audiation, not from the syllables (pp. 111–117).

terms.title: Symbolic association
terms.short: MLT level 4: read and write the notation of patterns you can already audiate and name.
terms.long: Notation is "a 'window' one sees through. Audiation is on the other side" (p. 8). From about p. 117.

terms.title: Composite synthesis
terms.short: MLT level 5: read and write series of patterns and recognize their tonality or meter in notation.
terms.long: From p. 126.

terms.title: Generalization
terms.short: MLT inference level: identify unfamiliar patterns by ear, by name or in notation, using what you know.
terms.long: Sublevels: aural/oral, verbal and symbolic (reading and writing) (pp. 129–133).

terms.title: Creativity/improvisation
terms.short: MLT inference level: make up your own music, by ear or in notation, from patterns you audiate.
terms.long: Gordon recommends bridging to this level "as soon as students are ready" (p. 231). From p. 136.

terms.title: Theoretical understanding
terms.short: MLT inference level: explain why music works as it does, the last level, built on audiation.
terms.long: Music theory comes at the end of the sequence, not the beginning (p. 106). From about p. 141.
